title: Report a result from a table
objective: Compare values with their units and explain one limit of the evidence.

slides.title: Read the label before the number
body: Find what was measured, the groups, and the unit.
Look for a pattern. Give values to support your comparison. Keep a possible explanation for the discussion.

slides.title: Write about a catalase table
body: Simulated values from the class exercise: mean oxygen in the first minute was 8.3 mL at pH 4 and 13.9 mL at pH 5.
Model: The mean was 5.6 mL higher at pH 5 than at pH 4.
Point to the two values used in the comparison.

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Classroom data: Students counted birds for ten minutes per site. Pond = 12 birds. Garden = 8 birds. Field = 4 birds. They visited each site once.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: What did the students measure? Give the unit and the time for each site.
Compare the highest and lowest sites. Use both counts and give the difference.
Look for the animal, the number, and the time.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Classroom data: Students counted butterflies for ten minutes per site. Park = 15 butterflies. Garden = 10 butterflies. Field = 5 butterflies. They visited each site once.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: What did the students measure? Give the unit and the time for each site.
Compare the highest and lowest sites. Use both counts and give the difference.
A student says the highest site always has the most animals. What can you say from these data?

slides.title: Separate two statements
body: Say one result supported by the case. Then say one thing we would need to learn from a second visit.
